question: Does retaining each worker's Neumaier (sum, compensation) state preserve a correctly rounded result under actual OS-thread scheduling, and how do wall time, aggregate process CPU time, and Python-traced peak memory differ between GIL-enabled and free-threaded CPython?

layouts.grouped_cancellation: [1e16] repeated N, then [1.0] repeated N, then [-1e16] repeated N

synthetic_input.binary64_reference: float of the exact rational sum of the represented binary64 inputs

execution.thread_identity: threading.get_native_id; the run fails if configured workers do not execute on distinct native threads
execution.gil_state: sys._is_gil_enabled() plus sysconfig.get_config_var('Py_GIL_DISABLED'); requested mode is asserted before measurement
execution.free_threaded_status: Officially supported as an optional CPython build starting with Python 3.14 (PEP 779); the GIL-enabled build remains the default.

measurement.cpu_time: median time.process_time_ns duration; process-wide user and system CPU time
measurement.parallelism_indicator: process CPU time divided by wall time; values above 1 can indicate aggregate CPU execution across threads but are not a portable speed guarantee
measurement.memory: tracemalloc peak delta during one invocation; excludes untracked native allocations and is not RSS
measurement.speedup: threaded median wall time compared with the matching serial algorithm baseline
measurement.accuracy: exact rational reference from the constructed represented binary64 inputs; count of measured runs equal to its binary64 rounding

merge_rules.scalar_partial: each worker returns one float; scalar partials are merged with math.fsum
merge_rules.compensation_state: each worker returns (sum, compensation); all components are merged with Neumaier compensation

validation: assert GIL-enabled and free-threaded interpreter modes explicitly
record Python version, platform, architecture, CPU count and CPU affinity when available
record input SHA-256 for canonical big-endian binary64 values
require one distinct native thread per configured worker
run unit tests for exact reference, partitions, state merge and result metadata
do not impose universal performance thresholds
limitations: synthetic cancellation workloads only; no production scientific dataset
one Ubuntu x86_64 CI host family; no ARM or Windows/macOS threaded benchmark in this cycle
free-threaded CPython remains an evolving runtime mode and may have workload-dependent overhead
thread pool startup and scheduling are included in the measured operation
process CPU time is process-wide and can be affected by host scheduling and CPU quotas
tracemalloc measures Python-traced allocations, not total RSS or every native allocation
no GPU, NumPy/BLAS, OpenMP, process pool or network-distributed execution is tested
The CI matrix pins CPython 3.14.4/3.14.4t; as of 2026-11-25 the latest 3.14 patch is 3.14.10, so current-patch replication remains outstanding.
